newsitem.title: UK: UK rate rise shows economic weakness - Labour.
newsitem.headline: UK rate rise shows economic weakness - Labour.

text.p: Wednesday's quarter-point rise in interest rates illustrates the fundamental, underlying weakness of Britain's economy, Gordon Brown, economics spokesman for the main opposition Labour party, told BBC television.

Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke, who earlier raised official interest rates to six percent from 5.75 percent, had failed to address weaknesses in the economy "which have meant that this is not an industry-led or investment- or export-led recovery," Brown said.
He said voters would conclude that the ruling Conservatives' economic mismanagement had led to high interest rates.
"They are now giving us higher inflation than our competitors and they have not made the fundamental changes that can give us long-term sustainable growth," Brown added.
Malcolm Bruce, economics spokesman of the Liberal Democrats, also blamed the Conservatives for failing to ensure adequate investment in the economy.
"It shows that the economic policies of the last 17 years have failed to deliver strength in the British economy that can enable us to grow without hitting inflation," he told BBC television.
